deepdive.sec: Steel & Alloy Castings (engineering-led) / Mining-Earthmoving-Construction & Locomotive Capital-Goods

bull_bear.body:
- Debt-free balance sheet, ~₹114 cr cash — funding capex internally.
- **Bonus issue:** investor-prompted; management said "nothing on the horizon" but is "thinking" — no commitment.
- Dividend not specifically quantified on the call.
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation

bull_bear.body:
- **YoY-quarter decline** (Q4FY26 ~12% below Q4FY25) — volume moderation vs prior year; mgmt downplays as "aberration."
- **Railroad component issues unresolved** — execution risk in one of the five target verticals.
- **Customer/geography concentration** historically a concern (investor flagged); diversification still in progress; no sector/geo revenue split disclosed yet (promised from Q1FY27).
- **Fuel/freight/RM inflation & Middle-East (Iran-U.S.) conflict** delaying orders (incl. defence) and raising costs; mitigated but not eliminated by cost-plus pass-through (lag) and FX.
- **Capex timing/sizing undisclosed** — execution and demand-visibility dependence.
- Cyclicality of end-user industries; FX exposure on >60% exports.
bull_bear.title: Risks & watch-items

bull_bear.body:
- Confident, disciplined, conservative on guidance (insists on annual-not-quarterly framing; resets margin expectation *down* to 25–26% despite delivering 30%+ — under-promise posture).
- Transparent on cost pressures and pass-through mechanics; candid that defence is de-emphasised and that data-centers are irrelevant to its product (refreshingly non-hype).
- Accepts investor suggestion to add sector/geo revenue disclosure from Q1FY27 — responsive on governance/disclosure.
bull_bear.title: Management quality / tone

bull_bear.body:
- The "20% growth" is **volume**, not value — value growth could differ given price pass-throughs; investors conflating the two may over/under-estimate revenue.
- Management actively **cooled the data-center narrative** that a large client had stoked — signals candour but also caps a speculative re-rating angle.
- The ">₹100 cr PAT FY27" and "double sales by FY29 (~₹860 cr)" are explicitly **aspirations**, not guidance — and the ₹860 cr is achievable *within present capacity* (heavy operating leverage if utilisation climbs from ~63% toward full).
- Capex pulled forward to July despite sub-75% utilisation = early-cycle conviction signal on demand.
bull_bear.title: Non-obvious takeaways

bull_bear.body:
- Deck explicitly lists debt-free status as a moat; finance costs were negligible at Rs 0.3 crore in FY26 versus Rs 0.7 crore in FY25.
- The ~Rs 120 crore greenfield capex is being funded off this debt-free balance sheet and phased over two years rather than in one hit.
- Returns profile cited at 28.6% RoCE and 22.0% RoE in FY26, down from the FY23 peak of 43.7% / 32.8% as the asset base and cash build.
- Capital is also being cycled into captive renewable generation, which converts capex into a recurring operating cost saving.
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation policy (investor deck)

business.body:
- Standalone business; no subsidiaries discussed.
- Core end-markets: **mining, earthmoving, construction, locomotives/railroad, ground engaging tools.** These five are the stated growth engines.
- **Railroad/locomotive:** certain critical components still "under stress" — developments not yet fully resolved; competitive intensity in railroad less favourable than the other segments, so focus tilted to mining/earthmoving/construction.
- **Exports >60% of revenue** (FY26); steady traction from North America & developed markets via OEM supply-chain diversification.

business.body:
- Claims a premier position in India's steel casting industry and is one of the few companies in India and globally making structural steel castings via the sand and shell casting process, competing with global players.
- Serves a marquee multinational OEM base including Fortune 500 customers across earth moving, mining and mineral processing, locomotives, rail-road, construction, cement, transport, defence and GETs — nine sectors in all.
- Deck frames the China+1 sourcing shift as a structural tailwind making Steelcast a preferred supplier, supported by a balanced domestic-plus-export customer portfolio and six decades of surviving business cycles.
- Export footprint spans 16 countries (USA, Mexico, Brazil, Canada, Denmark, Germany, Poland, Slovakia, Israel, South Korea, China, Japan, Singapore, Australia, Thailand, India base), targeted to reach 18+ countries in the next 1-2 years; holds Two-Star Export House status.
business.title: Positioning (investor deck)

business.body:
- [Certifications] R&D laboratory approved by the Department of Science & Technology, Government of India, supporting the deck's claim of strong R&D and technological capabilities as an entry barrier.
- [Governance] Deck highlights a well-experienced team and a balanced/professional board as part of the moat; investor relations is run through EY, with ED & CFO Mr. Subhash Sharma as the named contact.
business.title: Notable from the deck

latest_quarter.body:
- FY26 EBITDA margin 30.64% (+104 bps); near-term Q4 pressure from fuel/power, maintenance, export-obligation provisions.
- **Cost-plus / sales-price-variation formula** with all customers → RM/fuel cost increases passed through (auto formula, both directions). ~10% RM rise from Mar-1 → ~4–5% price pass-through; partial from Apr-1, balance from Jul-1.
- Rupee depreciation + >60% export mix act as natural cushions.
- Sustainable-margin frame reset lower (25–26% EBITDA) for conservative modelling despite recent 28–30%+ prints.
latest_quarter.title: Margins & cost dynamics

latest_quarter.body: - **Q4 FY26 (this):** FY26 rev ₹423.17cr (+13.3%), EBITDA ₹129.64cr (30.64% margin, +104bps), PAT ₹86.86cr (+20.3%). Q4 rev ₹112.43cr (+15.4% QoQ) but ~12% below Q4FY25. Order book ~₹130–135cr (1-Apr). Cash ~₹114cr, debt-free. Capex decision advanced to end-July 2026 (from Dec-26); size undisclosed. Util ~63–64%. New margin frame: sustainable EBITDA 25–26%. Aspirations: >₹100cr PAT FY27, double volumes (~₹860cr) by FY29 within present capacity, 20%+ volume CAGR. GET 1.1%→3.8% of sales FY27. 2.4MW hybrid power live by Jun-26 (~₹3.6cr/yr savings). Data-center demand explicitly ruled out; defence de-emphasised (₹15–18cr repeat-order optionality). Railroad components still under stress. Sector/geo revenue split disclosure promised from Q1FY27.
latest_quarter.title: QoQ change log

outlook.body:
- **Revenue/volume growth:** ~**20%+ CAGR over next 3 years (through FY29), specifically FY27**. NOTE mgmt clarified the 20% refers to **volume growth**, not value.
- **Doubling aspiration:** Double volumes within *present capacity* → theoretically **~₹860 cr revenue by FY29** vs FY26 ₹423 cr.
- **PAT goal:** Aspiration to be a **">₹100 cr PAT company in FY27"** (could be ₹101cr or ₹115cr — framed as aspiration, not formal guidance; FY26 base ₹86.86 cr).
- **Margin:** Sustainable **EBITDA 25–26%** over the long term (may touch ~30% at times, but advised modelling 25–26%); historical band 28–30% EBITDA / 18–20% PAT.
- **Capacity utilisation:** FY26 ~**63–64%**; will NOT wait for 75% before adding capacity given strong customer indications.
- **Capex decision:** To be finalised by **end-July 2026** (advanced stage); originally contemplated for Dec-2026 but pulled forward. Project cost / size not yet disclosed.
- **GET contribution:** 1.1% of sales in FY26 → targeted **3.8% in FY27** (from existing customers).
- **Hybrid power:** 2.4 MW hybrid project commissioning by **June 2026**, ~₹3.6 cr/yr savings.
outlook.title: Guidance (CRITICAL)

outlook.body:
- Opening order book ~**₹130–135 cr** as of 1-Apr-2026; conversion cycle ~110–120 days (roughly one quarter's revenue visibility).
- **50+ new parts** under various development stages (constant pipeline); approval pace *rose* in last 4–6 weeks despite geopolitics. New-part flow spans full 5 kg–2,500 kg weight range.
- Overseas **defence repeat order**: prototypes approved (compact vehicles for ground wars), awaiting serial-supply orders (delayed by Iran-U.S. situation); potential **₹15–18 cr** sales if it converts.
outlook.title: Order book & pipeline

outlook.body:
- **China+1 / OEM outsourcing** — primary structural driver; global OEMs increasingly outsourcing specialised high-performance castings.
- **Ground Engaging Tools (GET)** — scaling 1.1%→3.8% of sales into FY27; optionality to grow further.
- **Overseas defence** — kept as opportunistic (₹15–18 cr potential), management has deliberately de-prioritised it.
- **Data centers — explicitly ruled out**: management says steel castings have practically no data-center application.
outlook.title: Growth verticals / optionality

deepdive.thesis: Debt-free, ~60%+ export steel-casting niche play riding global OEM outsourcing/China+1 with 30%+ EBITDA margins and a stated 20%+ volume CAGR aspiration to FY29 (double sales to ~₹860cr) plus a ">₹100cr PAT in FY27" goal — near-term margin wobble from fuel/freight/RM inflation is being passed through under cost-plus formulas.

open.item: US tariffs raise end-customer costs and are causing near-term demand softness; management flags the conclusion of the India-US trade deal by end-November as the key watch item for normalisation from Q4FY26.

The railroad component has repeatedly failed field-life trials and remains unapproved; management expects to resolve it in the next 1-2 quarters with a stated success probability of more than 85%, and it is excluded from FY26 growth guidance.

The company is evaluating two expansion options - replicating current capacity on the China Plus One theme, or moving into heavier piece weights of 2.5 to 6 tons versus the current 2.5 ton limit - with visibility expected in the next 3-4 quarters.
Exports currently go to about 15 countries and are likely to extend to 18 countries within another one or two quarters.
FY26 capacity utilisation guidance revised down from 53% to around 48-49% due to tariff issues.

After shipping 250 approved prototypes in June and 2,000 units in September that reach the overseas customer by mid-November for 10-12 weeks of testing, management expects additional defence export volumes from Q4FY26 or Q1FY27.
open.promised: 2,000 units shipped; follow-on order expected count

open.item: The next capacity expansion decision has been deferred and will be reviewed around end of FY26, to be triggered at an appropriate time.
FY26 revenue growth guidance cut from the earlier 18-20% to double-digit growth of around 12% because of US tariff-related disruption.
Management expects a softer Q3FY26 on weak demand visibility and geopolitical uncertainty, with Q4FY26 performing better than Q3FY26 if the US trade deal concludes by end-November.
Management guided to 18-20% revenue growth in FY26 over FY25, explicitly excluding any contribution from the pending railroad component.
A 2.4 MW hybrid power plant under the group captive model is to be commissioned on or before 31 March 2026.
FY26 capacity utilisation guidance was cut to about 53% from the earlier 57-59% because of slower OEM decision-making after the US tariffs.
FY26 capex plan of acquiring 100,000 sq m of Gujarat government land plus debottlenecking investments is on track with no change in execution.

FY26 capex of Rs 27 crore, mainly for debottlenecking and purchase of land for future investments.
